title: Bounded-below direct-image cohomology is a sheafified inverse-image presheaf
statement: Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal R$ a sheaf of rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the chosen small sites and universes [def-weil-size-convention]. The direct image of $\mathcal R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] takes values in modules over $f_*\mathcal R$, with $(f_*M)(V)=M(X\times_YV)$ [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image]; write $Rf_*$ for its total right derived functor [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. For a bounded-below complex $K^\bullet$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of $\mathcal R$-modules and an integer $q$, define an abelian presheaf on $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$ by $P_K^q(V)=H^q(X\times_YV,K^\bullet)$, where $H^q(U,K^\bullet)$ means the cohomology of the right-derived section-evaluation functor $M\mapsto M(U)$ on $\mathcal R$-modules. Restriction maps are those of derived section evaluation. There is a canonical isomorphism of abelian sheaves, using sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], $(P_K^q)^\#\cong\mathcal H^q(Rf_*K^\bullet)$, with the right side read as its underlying abelian sheaf. This isomorphism is natural in $K^\bullet$ and identifies the maps induced by every morphism of complexes with the corresponding maps of sheafified presheaves.

source.place: Tag 0D6I, lemma-unbounded-describe-higher-direct-images; specialize the ringed-site morphism to the pro-etale geometric morphism with target coefficient sheaf f_*R and its counit to R (bounded-below case).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], the category of left $\mathcal R$-modules on the chosen small pro-etale site of $X$ is Grothendieck abelian; this statement allows noncommutative rings. Apply [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] to choose a quasi-isomorphism $s:K\to I$ with $I$ K-injective. By [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], $Rf_*K$ is canonically represented by $f_*I$. The same definition applied to each additive evaluation functor $\Gamma(U,-):M\mapsto M(U)$ gives $R\Gamma(U,K)\cong I(U)$, hence $H^q(U,K)=H^q(I(U))$. All these evaluations use the single resolution $I$, and restriction maps are obtained by evaluating its terms.

source.place: Tags 079Q (remark-existence-D) and 079P (theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck); computation as in sites-cohomology.tex, proof of lemma-sheafification-cohomology

proof.text: Put $u(V)=X\times_YV$. By [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image], precomposition with $u$ sends sheaves to sheaves and $(f_*I)^n(V)=I^n(u(V))$, with restrictions induced by $u$. Equip this sheaf with its $f_*\mathcal R$-action term by term: $r\in\mathcal R(u(V))$ acts on $I^n(u(V))$ by the given module action. The module axioms and compatibility with restrictions and differentials are precisely those of $I$. Let $B$ be the underlying abelian sheaf complex of $f_*I$, and $A$ its underlying presheaf complex. Then $A^n(V)=I^n(u(V))$ and the cohomology presheaf $H^q(A)$ is $P_K^q$, since both are the sectionwise quotient $\ker(d^q_V)/\operatorname{im}(d^{q-1}_V)$ with the same restriction maps.

Abelian presheaf sheafification is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to this exact functor and the presheaf complex $A$: $(H^q(A))^\#\cong H^q(A^\#)$, naturally in chain maps. Since the terms of $B$ are sheaves, their sheafifications are canonically themselves by the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], explicitly, the identity of each sheaf $B^n$ extends uniquely to $e_n:(A^n)^\#\to B^n$. If $a_n:B^n\to(A^n)^\#$ is the sheafification unit, then $e_na_n=1$, and $a_ne_n=1$ since both endomorphisms of $(A^n)^\#$ have the same composite with $a_n$. This extension is natural: the two composites for any map $B^n\to B^m$ agree after the unit and hence agree by uniqueness. In particular the $e_n$ commute with differentials, giving $A^\#\cong B$ as complexes. Moreover [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](1), applied on $Y$ with ring $f_*\mathcal R$, says that forgetting the module action is exact. The same exact-functor cohomology comparison identifies $H^q(B)$ with the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal H^q(f_*I)$. Thus $(P_K^q)^\#\cong\mathcal H^q(Rf_*K)$ as abelian sheaves. On a sectionwise cycle this is the map induced by the sheafification unit and projection to sheaf cohomology.

source.place: Proof of lemma-sheafification-cohomology, kernel/image quotient; sites-modules.tex Tags 03DA and 03CO

proof.text: Use the published functorial K-injective replacement on the small model and transport it to the original site. The augmentation is a natural transformation, so for a chain map t:K→L its resolution map g:I→J satisfies t ≫ r = s ≫ g. Expand the canonical right-derived comparison as RF(Qs), the quotient-presentation comparison, and the inverse unit at I. Functoriality, naturality of the quotient comparison and naturality of the derived unit prove RF(Qt) ≫ c_r = c_s ≫ Q(Fg). The exact-functor homology comparisons are natural by ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso_hom_naturality. The pointwise homology comparison is natural both in site arrows and in maps of complexes. Compose these natural isomorphisms with the sheafification counit and with the inverse of the derived-resolution comparison. Their components are exactly the originally specified boundedComplexDirectImagePresheafIso. The naturality of their composite is the asserted square. No choice of chain-map representatives is required, because the resolution was functorial from the outset.
